title: Simplifying the running jargon: Training pace
claims: England Athletics describes easy running as a fully conversational, relaxed pace corresponding to 60–75% of maximum heart rate, or RPE 2–3 out of 10.
Steady-state running is described as harder than easy running but still under control, at RPE 4–5.
Threshold running is described as comfortably hard, just below the point where lactate builds up, at RPE 7–8 with only one-word answers possible.
Interval training is described as blocks of high-intensity work with rest, generally between 3 km and 10 km race pace.
The article notes that the science and technology to measure threshold level is not available to all, so running pace is determined more by feel than science.
The guidance gives heart-rate percentages and RPE anchors but no percentage-based table for deriving training paces from a race result.

正文只在 easy 跑给出 60-75% HRmax，其余区间用 RPE；全文没有由比赛成绩推导训练配速的百分比表。
